html:
SMTO-EXE-0210 — The saved password didn't unlock this PDF

GUID: 88605b18-84de-5f40-8327-f43cec4b087d
Slug: pdf-password-invalid
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: pdf

What happened

  • This PDF is password-protected, and the password SMTO used from your saved PDF password didn't open it. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check the password by opening the PDF in your usual PDF viewer and typing it in. This confirms which password actually opens the file.
  2. Open Parameter Store, select the PDF password you used, enter the correct password, and select Save. SMTO takes the password from this saved entry, never from the chat.
  3. Send SMTO a new message that mentions the saved password with @ followed by its name, and ask for the PDF action again. SMTO picks up the corrected password only when a new message mentions it.

What success looks like

  • SMTO opens the PDF and completes the action you asked for.

If it still fails

  • If you don't know the right password, ask whoever sent you the PDF. If the correct password still fails, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't type the password into the chat; keep it in Parameter Store.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The password supplied through the accepted pdf_password reference failed the encrypted PDF's decryption check.

What this means

  • An explicitly supplied private password failed the encrypted document's decryption check. PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.

Why this can happen

  • An explicitly supplied private password failed the encrypted document's decryption check.

How to diagnose it

  • Verify the intended document and accepted password-profile revision without exposing the credential or retrying guessed values.

How to fix it

  • Correct the value of the pdf_password parameter in Parameter Store, then submit a new prompt that mentions it so the new revision is accepted, and retry with that key as password_ref. Accepted bindings are captured when the task starts, so a running task keeps the old value.
  • Correct the private pdf_password parameter, accept its new revision, and retry with password_ref.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the private pdf_password parameter, accept its new revision, and retry with password_ref.

How to verify the fix

  • The corrected accepted private reference unlocks the intended document with the required rights.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
